verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a single docs mention that npm creates a lock file and installs from it even after switching registries. That implies per-project dependency pinning, but nothing documents exact-version specifiers or how strictly installs respect the pins. A community mention of `npm ci` gives no detail on lockfile enforcement. Missing for 10: documentation of exact-version pinning in package.json, documented lockfile-respecting install behavior (e.g. npm ci failing on mismatch), per-project pinning of tools or the Node/npm version, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pin exact versions of packages and tools per project and have the manager respect those pins

citations.quote: If you create a lock file while using the default registry you can switch to another registry and npm will install packages from the new registry
